messages.subject: DPA Review — Art.28 Requirements
messages.body: [Email Dr. Sarah Chen → VendorX Legal Thu Jan 12 2026] Per GDPR Article 28(3), the DPA must be in writing (including electronic form) and must address all mandatory elements. We have identified a gap in the current DPA v1.2: the sub-processor authorisation mechanism is not adequately specified. GDPR Art.28(3)(d) requires prior specific or general written authorisation for sub-processors. The current draft (§3.4) acknowledges this requirement but does not provide a mechanism for 'general written authorisation' of sub-processor categories. Please revise. Note: Non-compliance with Art.28 may result in penalties up to €10,000,000 or 2% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher.

messages.subject: RE: DPA Review — Art.28 Requirements
messages.body: [Email VendorX Legal → Dr. Sarah Chen Sat Jan 14 2026] Thank you for your detailed review. We acknowledge the sub-processor gap you identified in DPA §3.4. We will provide a revised DPA with a general authorisation mechanism (list of pre-approved sub-processors with a change notification procedure) in our next draft. We will target delivery with the MSA v2.4 package. Separately, we note your point on the CISG exclusion. Our legal team confirms that the MSA §12.3 CISG exclusion is valid and effective under Dutch law as well. VendorX agrees CISG does not apply.
